findings.title: Deleting calendar cache does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `showToast` and the optional `onSuccess` callback, without invalidating `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation` below it, which calls `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`). Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.useQuery` and its `onChanged` prop is optional, the UI keeps the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` value after cache deletion and continues showing the old cache timestamp and the "Delete cached data" action until the page is manually refreshed.

findings.title: connectedCalendarsHandler bypasses CalendarCache.init and always queries the database
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of using `await CalendarCache.init(null)`. `CalendarCache.init` checks whether the `calendar-cache` feature is enabled and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when it is disabled. Instantiating `CalendarCacheRepository` directly makes the newly added `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method unreachable and executes the `calendarCache.groupBy` query even when the calendar cache feature is disabled.

findings.title: Unused SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on cache refresh and extra fields in session query
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` executes `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` across all selected calendars for the credential, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` (in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`) was updated to select `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every session lookup. Since cache status is read from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`cacheUpdatedAt`) rather than `SelectedCalendar`, these leftover changes perform an unnecessary `UPDATE` on every cache refresh and fetch unused fields on every authenticated session check.

findings.title: Webhook test script writes to ../.env relative to caller working directory and uses macOS-only sed
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's current working directory rather than the script's directory (`$(dirname "$0")/../.env`), so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root creates or modifies `../.env` outside the repository. In addition, line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E`, which is BSD/macOS-specific and fails under GNU `sed` on Linux.
